A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EmbQA research work. All 14 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA accuracy, runtime, retrieval coverage and component-ablation results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, threshold experiments, component analyses, stage-level costs and GPT-4o-mini results.

M1.justification: The full EmbQA algorithm, losses and exploratory-embedding reader remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a limited adaptation that combines the existing EmbQA reranker with SuRe for GPT-4o-mini, allowing reranking without the full pipeline's internal reader operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HotpotQA, 2Wiki, Natural Questions and WebQuestions with the same described retrieval corpora. Added studies reuse this coverage; GPT-4o-mini introduces a model configuration rather than different data or QA requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated RPG and KnowTrace comparisons under the retained LLaMA 3.1, BM25 and top-10 setup. These extend the substantive comparison to iterative planning and knowledge-tracing approaches. Existing baselines and the prompt-level reranker comparison are retained.

E3.justification: Original evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added protocols use HotpotQA as development data for thresholds 0.05, 0.01, 0.005 and 0.001, introduce a direct-summation control without contrastive learning, and evaluate GPT-4o-mini with Contriever. These are targeted extensions, not documented revisions of the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds model-wise retrieval and entropy diagnostics plus threshold sensitivity experiments. Appendix D isolates the contribution of contrastive learning against direct embedding summation, and Appendix E decomposes runtime and token costs by stage. These substantially expand the mechanism and efficiency analyses beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or a specified significance-testing procedure; Figure 3 retains its 200 samples. Appendix C adds nonsignificance assertions without documenting a test. Table 8's predictive entropy measures model confidence rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Existing matched table and figure results are retained apart from rounding, while v2 adds substantial results in Table 1 and Tables 7–12. For example, Table 12 reports average EM/F1 of 41.6/54.5 for GPT-4o-mini with SuRe and 43.9/56.9 with the added reranker. These are newly reported configurations, not improved scores for v1's original model settings.

T1.justification: Section 3's mathematical definitions and Appendix B's Gaussian assumptions, order-statistic reasoning and inequalities are unchanged in substance. Edits are linguistic and typographical; the new lower-bound discussion supplies no additional derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about embedding-based reranking, exploratory generation, and improved accuracy and efficiency. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 attributes modest Mistral/Qwen gains to overconfidence and questions a universal threshold, interprets the new control as evidence for contrastive learning, and explains efficiency through prompting stages. Appendix F qualifies the API restriction by distinguishing the reranker from the full pipeline. Appendix C also introduces significance and performance-lower-bound assertions without corresponding tests or proofs.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly documents the seven-versus-two prompting stages and their individual time/token costs. Appendix D specifies direct vector summation for its control. Existing implementation settings, Appendix A prompts and tool-access URLs remain unchanged; no new code release or detailed training recipe is provided.

R1.justification: Section 2 more explicitly positions EmbQA within retrieval-augmented generation, adding Atlas and Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation. RPG and KnowTrace are also newly cited and evaluated. The central positioning against prompt-level approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes light grammatical and spelling edits, rewrites selected related-work and results paragraphs, updates acknowledgments, and organizes new explanations into Appendices C–F. The main section sequence and most existing methodological and theoretical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with Tables 7–12 covering diagnostics, thresholds, ablations, costs and API results, while Table 1 gains comparator rows. v1's full-width Appendix Table 6 becomes the compact main-text Table 5; candidate coverage becomes Table 6. Figures 1–3 retain their artwork, and Table 10 partly redisplays Figure 2 results.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, contrastive-learning control, threshold sweep and stage-cost breakdown make competitiveness, component contributions and efficiency more assessable; the API experiment also clarifies partial applicability. These benefits are limited by Appendix C's unsupported overconfidence, significance and lower-bound interpretations. Section 4.2 additionally claims a 66% call reduction despite specifying seven versus two calls, which implies 71.4%. The revision provides useful additional evidence without resolving these explanatory weaknesses.
